segments.caption: A person documents the installation of a beehive in a tree, beginning with a shot of the tree on April 4, 2013, when a swarm is said to have moved in. On April 10, 2013, six days later, the person is shown opening the hive by cutting a circular hole in the tree trunk and securing it with rope, marking the first opening.
A beekeeper inspects a newly established beehive, opening a tree trunk to reveal a dense cluster of bees and their brood, marking the hive's first inspection six days after its creation.
A person opens a tree cavity 17 days after the bees' emergence to reveal a dense, thriving colony of bees actively covering the inner surfaces, showcasing their rapid growth and organized structure.

A close-up view captures a dense, living bee swarm clinging to the rough, textured surface of a tree trunk, with a hand shown holding a rope tied around the tree, indicating an ongoing observation or management effort.
A beekeeper inspects a large, active swarm of bees clustered inside a hollow tree, pointing to the cavity where the colony is nestled, indicating the successful location and capture of the swarm.

A person carefully removes a circular section of bark from a large tree trunk, revealing a dense swarm of bees nestled inside the hollow cavity. After extracting the wooden disc, the bees are seen swarming over its surface before the disc is set aside, leaving the tree cavity empty and the rope used for the extraction visible against the rough bark.

The video opens on a large, rough-barked tree trunk secured with thick ropes, establishing the location as an outdoor, natural setting. The camera then moves into the hollow of the tree, revealing a thriving, dense bee colony nestled within. Thousands of bees swarm over the honeycomb structures, actively tending to the wax cells and moving in constant, bustling motion.
